rows.feature: Invite to Portal on the project page
rows.what: An outline button in the project header (in the ⋯ menu below desktop width) opens the Invite to Portal dialog for the project's client.
rows.v1: Project › header › Invite to Portal (⋯ › Invite to Portal on smaller screens)
rows.v2: Project › ⋮ › Invite to Portal; Overview › Getting started › Invite the client; Projects listing › row ⋮; a Choice or Schedule share offers it when the client isn't invited
rows.how: Not a header button: the ⋮ and several doors open one Invite to Portal side panel, which also shows who can open the page, what they see, what waits on them, and lets you withdraw access.

rows.feature: Invite to Portal from the lead
rows.what: The lead drawer's Invite to Portal opens the same dialog for a lead that is not yet a project.
rows.v1: Leads › lead drawer › Invite to Portal
rows.v2: Lead › ⋮ › Invite to Portal

rows.feature: Invite form: the client's name and phone with a country code
rows.what: The studio types the homeowner's name and phone (dial-code picker per country); the name typed overwrites the client's portal profile.
rows.v1: Invite to Portal dialog › Homeowner Name · Phone Number
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel (no form — the client's name and number come from the lead or project)
rows.how: Nothing is typed: the invite goes to the record's own client. Singapore mobile numbers only; a landline is refused before WhatsApp opens. A wrong number is fixed on the lead.

rows.feature: Send the invite on WhatsApp
rows.what: Send via WhatsApp opens wa.me from the designer's own WhatsApp with a ready message holding the studio's sign-in link, with a fallback when the pop-up is blocked.
rows.v1: Invite to Portal dialog › Send via WhatsApp
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel › Invite on WhatsApp

rows.feature: Copy the portal link
rows.what: Copy Link puts the studio's sign-in address on the clipboard.
rows.v1: Invite to Portal dialog › Copy Link
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel › Their page › Copy

rows.feature: Send the link again
rows.what: Pressing Invite again for an invited client simply opens a fresh WhatsApp draft (“already invited — resend”).
rows.v1: Invite to Portal dialog › Send via WhatsApp (again)
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel › Send the link on WhatsApp; the client's line then reads “sent again {day}”

rows.feature: See whether the client was invited and has opened the portal
rows.what: 1.0 showed no invited or opened state anywhere; it only stored a last-seen time the studio never saw.
rows.v1: Nowhere (header button always read Invite to Portal; Project Links showed no state)
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel and Company › Client portal › Clients: Not invited · Invited, not opened · Opened {when} · Withdrawn {day}, with who invited and when
rows.how: 2.0 shows the state on a chip and the date and inviter on the client's line.

rows.feature: Who may invite a client
rows.what: Any signed-in studio member could invite any client of the studio; no role check.
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel (read-only note for others)
rows.how: Only the client's team, their Manager, Owners and Admins invite, resend or withdraw, checked on the server; everyone else reads the panel.

rows.feature: Every lead with a phone gets portal access automatically
rows.what: A database trigger gave every lead with a phone an active portal link the moment it was saved, invited or not.
rows.how: Only a number the studio invited (and has not withdrawn) can sign in.

rows.feature: The lead's portal access carries into the project
rows.what: When a lead becomes a project the same portal link gets the project, so the client's sign-in keeps working.
rows.v2: Automatic: the project is the lead's second chapter; the household follows too

rows.feature: Show chat history to a newly invited person
rows.what: A switch on the invite decided whether the homeowner sees chat messages from before they joined.
rows.v1: Invite to Portal dialog › Show chat history
rows.how: The conversation belongs to the home; everyone in the household sees all of it.

rows.feature: The first invite opens the client's conversation
rows.what: The first invite created the project's client chat conversation if none existed.
rows.v2: Project › Client › Messages (always there, invite or not)
rows.how: Every project has its one conversation from the start; the invite creates nothing.

rows.feature: Preview as Homeowner
rows.what: A header button opened the homeowner's real project page in a new tab, read-only for 30 minutes, without the client's sign-in (but in practice needed a real homeowner session to render).
rows.v1: Project › header › Preview as Homeowner (⋯ below desktop)
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel › See it as {client} (and each household person's ⋮)
rows.how: Lives in the panel, not the header; lasts an hour; needs no client sign-in; only the client's team, Owners and Admins; a member who may not see money previews without Money; works for a lead-stage client too.

rows.feature: Preview bar and Close preview
rows.what: A sticky amber bar read “Preview as homeowner · Read-only” with Close preview.
rows.v1: Portal project page in preview › top bar
rows.v2: Portal preview › top strip “You're seeing {client}'s page as they see it…” › Close preview

rows.feature: Nothing pressed in a preview is saved
rows.what: Every write was refused in preview (server 403) and controls said a real homeowner login would do it.
rows.v2: Portal in preview (buttons off; every request refused on the server)

rows.feature: What a preview shows of the client's to-dos, bell and likes

rows.v2: Portal in preview › the bell reads as the client has it
rows.how: The bell and every page show what the client sees and mark nothing read; documents open the studio's own copy so no view is recorded as the client's.

rows.v2: Project › Schedule › What {client} sees pane; Share changes shows the copy that will go
rows.how: A pane beside the list and a preview inside Share changes instead of a dialog and a view switch.

rows.feature: Open as homeowner from the client directory

rows.v2: Company › Client portal › Clients › row ⋮ › See it as {client}; Company › Client portal › See it as {client}

rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › file ⋮ › Show to client (eye mark, Client column)

rows.feature: Only shared selections

notes: Verified against the 2.0 working tree on 2026-10-10 by reading code, nothing run; 1.0 rows come from inventories I and M, spot-checked in the 1.0 tree (routes, components and APIs under src/app/my, src/components/homeowner, src/app/api/homeowner*, src/app/api/portal, src/app/pay, tools/homeowner-portal). Skipped as dead in 1.0 (they did nothing there): the satisfaction rating route, the quote line-comment route, the preview-login-url route, the unused render-comment / moodboard / portfolio components, Quote Sharing Methods, and the four dead feature switches (Milestone Approvals, View and Sign Contracts, Auto-share Selections, Scope Details); motion and loader rows were left out. The studio side of render feedback (the Files & Docs panel, I-96…I-99) and the 1.0 floor-plan canvas itself (never read by inventory I) were left to their own areas. One defect found while mapping: the lead's Ask the client dialog still copies the mock's placeholder portal link and its Send via WhatsApp opens nothing (CP-110); the old InvitePortalModal that shares that placeholder is no longer mounted. The prototype holds one studio, so 1.0's per-studio session rules and the find-your-studio page have no 2.0 counterpart beyond the /my redirect (CP-044).
